claim: ESR1 is the key receptor underlying both estrogen-positive and -negative feedback in mice.
source: Studies in genetic mouse models have clearly identified that estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) is the key receptor underlying both estrogen-positive and -negative feedback (Couse et al., 2003; Herbison, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Couse et al., 2003 and Herbison, 2015

claim: GnRH neurons express ESR2 but not ESR1.
source: This is particularly intriguing given that the final output neuron of the network, the GnRH neuron, expresses ESR2 but not ESR1 (Herbison and Pape, 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Herbison and Pape, 2001

claim: Estradiol acts directly at ESR1-expressing kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus to suppress GnRH pulse generator activity and bring about estrogen-negative feedback.
source: Recent experiments using live cell imaging and in vivo CRISPR gene editing have demonstrated that estradiol acts directly at ESR1-expressing kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus to suppress the activity of the GnRH pulse generator and bring about estrogen-negative feedback at the level of the brain (McQuillan et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to McQuillan et al., 2022

claim: ESR1-expressing afferents to GnRH neuron cell bodies are concentrated in the AVPV and PVpo nuclei.
source: Viral retrograde labeling demonstrated that ESR1-expressing afferents to the GnRH neuron cell bodies are concentrated in the anteroventral periventricular (AVPV) and preoptic periventricular (PVpo) nuclei of the hypothalamus (Wintermantel et al., 2006); collectively termed the rostral periventricular area of the third ventricle (RP3V) (Herbison, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wintermantel et al., 2006 and Herbison, 2008

claim: Selective knockdown of ESR1 in the RP3V results in acyclic mice with an absent LH surge.
source: As the selective knockdown of ESR1 in the RP3V results in acyclic mice with an absent luteinizing hormone (LH) surge (Porteous and Herbison, 2019), it seems very likely that the RP3V is the area within which estradiol acts to enable the surge mechanism in mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Porteous and Herbison, 2019

claim: RP3V kisspeptin neurons express ESR1.
source: These cells express ESR1, are activated at the time of the surge, and have their kisspeptin synthesis strongly upregulated by estradiol (Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008

claim: RP3V kisspeptin neurons are activated at the time of the surge.
source: These cells express ESR1, are activated at the time of the surge, and have their kisspeptin synthesis strongly upregulated by estradiol (Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008

claim: Kisspeptin synthesis in RP3V neurons is strongly upregulated by estradiol.
source: These cells express ESR1, are activated at the time of the surge, and have their kisspeptin synthesis strongly upregulated by estradiol (Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2007; Clarkson et al., 2008

claim: RP3V kisspeptin neurons project directly to GnRH neuron cell bodies.
source: Further, RP3V kisspeptin neurons project directly to GnRH neuron cell bodies where they provide a strong and lasting excitatory influence while the selective activation of RP3V kisspeptin neurons in vivo evokes a surge-like increment in LH secretion (Piet et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Piet et al., 2018

claim: RP3V kisspeptin neurons provide a strong and lasting excitatory influence on GnRH neurons.
source: Further, RP3V kisspeptin neurons project directly to GnRH neuron cell bodies where they provide a strong and lasting excitatory influence while the selective activation of RP3V kisspeptin neurons in vivo evokes a surge-like increment in LH secretion (Piet et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Piet et al., 2018

claim: Selective activation of RP3V kisspeptin neurons in vivo evokes a surge-like increment in LH secretion.
source: Further, RP3V kisspeptin neurons project directly to GnRH neuron cell bodies where they provide a strong and lasting excitatory influence while the selective activation of RP3V kisspeptin neurons in vivo evokes a surge-like increment in LH secretion (Piet et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Piet et al., 2018

claim: Selective in vivo CRISPR knockdown of ESR1 in AVPV kisspeptin neurons blunted the amplitude of the LH surge but had no impact on estrous cyclicity.
source: Given these findings, it was surprising to find that selective in vivo CRISPR knockdown of ESR1 in AVPV kisspeptin neurons blunted the amplitude of the LH surge but had no impact on estrous cyclicity (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2019

claim: GABAA receptor transmission at GnRH neurons changes around the time of the daily LH surge.
source: This ranges from studies showing alterations in GABAA receptor transmission at GnRH neurons around the time of the daily LH surge (Christian and Moenter, 2007) to in vivo studies demonstrating a functionally significant fall in GABA release within the preoptic area just prior to the LH surge (Herbison and Dyer, 1991; Jarry et al., 1992).
evidence: Supported by citation to Christian and Moenter, 2007

claim: There is a functionally significant fall in GABA release within the preoptic area just prior to the LH surge.
source: This ranges from studies showing alterations in GABAA receptor transmission at GnRH neurons around the time of the daily LH surge (Christian and Moenter, 2007) to in vivo studies demonstrating a functionally significant fall in GABA release within the preoptic area just prior to the LH surge (Herbison and Dyer, 1991; Jarry et al., 1992).
evidence: Supported by citations to Herbison and Dyer, 1991; Jarry et al., 1992

claim: Genetic deletion of ESR1 in all GABA neurons results in failure of the positive feedback mechanism.
source: More recently, the genetic deletion of ESR1 in all GABA neurons was found to result in failure of the positive feedback mechanism (Cheong et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cheong et al., 2015

claim: gRNA-1, -2, -3, and -6 were the most effective in reducing Esr1 mRNA levels by 20–30% in vitro.
source: Transduction with AAV-U6-gRNA-EGFP identified gRNA-1, -2, -3, and -6 to be the most effective in reducing Esr1 mRNA levels by 20–30% in vitro.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from in vitro testing

claim: gRNA-2, -3, and -6 resulted in 79 ± 7%, 72 ± 5%, and 78 ± 3% reductions, respectively, in the numbers of ESR1-immunoreactive EGFP-expressing neurons on the injected side compared with the non-injected side.
source: This was found to result in 79 ± 7%, 72 ± 5%, and 78 ± 3% reductions, respectively, in the numbers of ESR1-immunoreactive EGFP-expressing neurons on the injected side of the brain compared with the non-injected side.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from in vivo testing in N=4 mice per gRNA

claim: Large numbers of cells expressing EGFP/Cas9 were detected throughout the preoptic area region, including the AVPV, PVpo, MPN, and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.
source: In keeping with the predominant GABAergic phenotype of preoptic area neurons (Moffitt et al., 2018), large numbers of cells expressing EGFP/Cas9 were detected throughout the region (Figure 1A and B), including the AVPV, PVpo, MPN, and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B and citation to Moffitt et al., 2018

claim: 52.1 ± 4.2% of VGAT-EGFP neurons expressed ESR1 in the MPN of mice that did not receive AAV injections.
source: Analyses of the MPN in mice that did not receive AAV injections found that 52.1 ± 4.2% of VGAT-EGFP neurons expressed ESR1 (N=12).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=12 mice

claim: In gRNA-LacZ mice, 54.9 ± 3.7% and 59.7 ± 3.9% of VGAT-EGFP neurons in the RP3V and MPN, respectively, were immunoreactive for ESR1.
source: In keeping with prior studies showing that up to one half of medial preoptic area GABA neurons express ESR1 (Herbison, 1997; Cheong et al., 2015), we found in gRNA-LacZ mice that 54.9 ± 3.7% and 59.7 ± 3.9% of VGAT-EGFP neurons in the RP3V (N=6) and MPN (N=7), respectively, were immunoreactive for ESR1 (Figure 1A and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=6-7 mice shown in Figure 1A and C, and citations to Herbison, 1997; Cheong et al., 2015

claim: In mice receiving gRNA-2, 23.1 ± 3.3% and 22.2 ± 4.7% of VGAT-EGFP neurons in the RP3V and MPN, respectively, were immunoreactive for ESR1.
source: In mice receiving gRNA-2, these values were reduced to 23.1 ± 3.3% (N=8) and 22.2 ± 4.7% (N=9) while gRNA-3 resulted in 17.6 ± 1.8% (N=8) and 19.3 ± 2.9% (N=8) of VGAT-EGFP neurons with ESR1 in the RP3V and MPN, respectively (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=8-9 mice shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: gRNA-3 resulted in 17.6 ± 1.8% and 19.3 ± 2.9% of VGAT-EGFP neurons with ESR1 in the RP3V and MPN, respectively.
source: In mice receiving gRNA-2, these values were reduced to 23.1 ± 3.3% (N=8) and 22.2 ± 4.7% (N=9) while gRNA-3 resulted in 17.6 ± 1.8% (N=8) and 19.3 ± 2.9% (N=8) of VGAT-EGFP neurons with ESR1 in the RP3V and MPN, respectively (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=8 mice shown in Figure 1B and C

claim: gRNA-2 and -3 generated a significant 62% and 68% reduction in ESR1 expression by RP3V VGAT neurons.
source: Overall, gRNA-2 and -3 generated a significant 62% and 68% reduction ESR1 expression by RP3V VGAT neurons (p<0.0001; one-way ANOVA F(2,19) = 41.91, post hoc Dunnett's test versus LacZ p<0.0001 [gRNA-2 and gRNA-3], Figure 1C) and a 63% and 71% reduction ESR1 expression by MPN VGAT neurons (p<0.0001; one-way ANOVA F(2,21) = 29.79, post hoc Dunnett's test versus LacZ p<0.0001 [gRNA-2 and gRNA-3], p<0.0001 [gRNA-3]; Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C

claim: gRNA-2 and -3 generated a 63% and 71% reduction in ESR1 expression by MPN VGAT neurons.
source: Overall, gRNA-2 and -3 generated a significant 62% and 68% reduction ESR1 expression by RP3V VGAT neurons (p<0.0001; one-way ANOVA F(2,19) = 41.91, post hoc Dunnett's test versus LacZ p<0.0001 [gRNA-2 and gRNA-3], Figure 1C) and a 63% and 71% reduction ESR1 expression by MPN VGAT neurons (p<0.0001; one-way ANOVA F(2,21) = 29.79, post hoc Dunnett's test versus LacZ p<0.0001 [gRNA-2 and gRNA-3], p<0.0001 [gRNA-3]; Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C

claim: Mean cycle length for all animals prior to AAV injection was 5.9±1.5 days.
source: Mean cycle length for all animals prior to AAV injection was 5.9±1.5 days.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from estrous cycle monitoring

claim: No significant differences were detected in cycle length for mice given gRNA-LacZ (n=6), gRNA-2 (N=7), or gRNA-3 (n=6).
source: No significant differences (p>0.05, Wilcoxon paired tests) were detected in cycle length for mice given gRNA-LacZ (n=6), gRNA-2 (N=7), or gRNA-3 (n=6) (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: Individual gRNA-LacZ mice exhibited relatively stable cycles before (5.9±0.7 days) and 3 weeks after (5.6±0.7 days) AAV injection.
source: Whereas individual gRNA-LacZ mice exhibited relatively stable cycles before (5.9±0.7 days) and 3 weeks after (5.6±0.7 days) AAV injection (Figure 2F), gRNA-2 and -3 mice displayed considerable variability in estrous cycle length after AAV injection with some mice entering constant estrous or diestrus (Figure 2G); scored as zero for cycle length.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F

claim: gRNA-2 and -3 mice displayed considerable variability in estrous cycle length after AAV injection with some mice entering constant estrous or diestrus.
source: Whereas individual gRNA-LacZ mice exhibited relatively stable cycles before (5.9±0.7 days) and 3 weeks after (5.6±0.7 days) AAV injection (Figure 2F), gRNA-2 and -3 mice displayed considerable variability in estrous cycle length after AAV injection with some mice entering constant estrous or diestrus (Figure 2G); scored as zero for cycle length.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G

claim: Four mice displaying constant estrous did not exhibit any unique gRNA, bilateral/unilateral injection location, or level of ESR1 in RP3V or MPN VGAT neurons.
source: The four mice displaying constant estrous did not exhibit any unique gRNA, bilateral/unilateral injection location, or level of ESR1 in RP3V or MPN VGAT neurons.
evidence: Supported by analysis of experimental data across multiple parameters

claim: All mice exhibited typical profiles of pulsatile LH secretion with the exception of three mice (one in each gRNA group) that had no LH pulse during the 180 min sampling period.
source: All mice exhibited typical profiles of pulsatile LH secretion (Figure 3A–D) with the exception of three mice (one in each gRNA group) that had no LH pulse during the 180 min sampling period.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-D

claim: gRNA-lacZ mice exhibited mean LH levels of 0.39±0.10 ng/mL and had LH pulses with an interval of 32.6±3.1 min and amplitude of 0.92±0.17 ng/mL.
source: The gRNA-lacZ mice exhibited mean LH levels of 0.39±0.10 ng/mL (n=6) and had LH pulses with an interval of 32.6±3.1 min and amplitude of 0.92±0.17 ng/mL (n=5), as found in wild-type mice (Czieselsky et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from n=5-6 mice and citation to Czieselsky et al., 2016

claim: No differences were detected in mean LH, pulse amplitude, or pulse interval between gRNA-LacZ and gRNA-2 or gRNA-3 mice.
source: No differences were detected in mean LH (p=0.35, H=2.17 Kruskal-Wallis test), pulse amplitude (p=0.034, H=6.26 with no post hoc differences between gRNA-LacZ and gRNA-2 [p=0.883, Dunn's test] or gRNA-3 [p=0.207]), or pulse interval (p=0.34, H=2.24) between gRNA-LacZ and gRNA-2 (n=6–7) or gRNA-3 mice (n=5–6) (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3E-G

claim: No significant correlations were detected between any pulse parameter and ESR1 expression in RP3V or MPN VGAT neurons.
source: No significant correlations were detected between any parameter in either region (Pearson correlation r values of 0.06–0.41; p>0.05) (Figure 3H–M).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3H-M

claim: All gRNA-lacZ mice had increased cFos expression in rostral preoptic area GnRH neurons (43 ± 8%, range 24–84%).
source: All gRNA-lacZ mice had increased cFos expression in rostral preoptic area GnRH neurons (43 ± 8%, range 24–84%; 21±0.7 GnRH neurons/section), although two of the mice had LH levels below 1.5 ng/mL indicating that they had likely surged before lights off (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B

claim: A significant reduction in the number of GnRH neurons with cFos was found with gRNA-2 but not gRNA-3 compared with gRNA-LacZ mice.
source: However, a significant reduction in the number GnRH neurons with cFos was found (p=0.0005, H=11.81 Kruskal-Wallis) with gRNA-2 (p=0.0023 Dunn's multiple comparisons) but not gRNA-3 (p=0.91) compared with gRNA-LacZ mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4A

claim: A significant correlation was found between ESR1 expression in RP3V VGAT neurons and cFos in GnRH neurons (p=0.008, Pearson r=0.66).
source: A significant correlation was found between ESR1 expression in RP3V VGAT neurons and cFos in GnRH neurons (p=0.008, Pearson r=0.66) (Figure 4C) but not LH secretion (p=0.26, Pearson r=0.31) across all mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4C

claim: No significant correlation was found between ESR1 expression in RP3V VGAT neurons and LH secretion (p=0.26, Pearson r=0.31).
source: A significant correlation was found between ESR1 expression in RP3V VGAT neurons and cFos in GnRH neurons (p=0.008, Pearson r=0.66) (Figure 4C) but not LH secretion (p=0.26, Pearson r=0.31) across all mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4D

claim: No significant correlation was found for ESR1 expression in MPN VGAT neurons and cFos in GnRH or LH secretion.
source: No significant correlation was found for ESR1 expression in MPN VGAT neurons and cFos in GnRH (p=0.18, Pearson r=0.36) or LH secretion (p=0.60, Pearson r=0.14) (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F

claim: The normal periventricular distribution of kisspeptin neurons was detected within the AVPV and PVpo of gRNA-lacZ mice with 20.1±2.0 and 24.0±1.9 kisspeptin cells/section, respectively.
source: The normal periventricular distribution of kisspeptin neurons was detected within the AVPV and PVpo of gRNA-lacZ mice (N=6) with 20.1±2.0 and 24.0±1.9 kisspeptin cells/section, respectively, and 74.5 ± 3.3% and 63.3 ± 5.1% of kisspeptin neurons positive for ESR1 immunoreactivity ('lacZ' group, Table 1; Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=6 mice shown in Table 1 and Figure 5

claim: In gRNA-lacZ mice, 74.5 ± 3.3% and 63.3 ± 5.1% of kisspeptin neurons in AVPV and PVpo, respectively, were positive for ESR1 immunoreactivity.
source: The normal periventricular distribution of kisspeptin neurons was detected within the AVPV and PVpo of gRNA-lacZ mice (N=6) with 20.1±2.0 and 24.0±1.9 kisspeptin cells/section, respectively, and 74.5 ± 3.3% and 63.3 ± 5.1% of kisspeptin neurons positive for ESR1 immunoreactivity ('lacZ' group, Table 1; Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from N=6 mice shown in Table 1 and Figure 5

claim: Four mice exhibited a near-complete lack of kisspeptin immunoreactivity within the entire RP3V.
source: Four mice exhibited a near-complete lack of kisspeptin immunoreactivity within the entire RP3V.
evidence: Supported by experimental observation in four mice

claim: RP3V kisspeptin neurons are a GABAergic phenotype.
source: As the RP3V kisspeptin neurons are a GABAergic phenotype (Moffitt et al., 2018), they will all be targeted for Cas9 expression in Vgat-Cas9 mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Moffitt et al., 2018

claim: 20–75% of RP3V kisspeptin neurons express Vgat in adult mice.
source: Prior estimates have indicated that 20–75% of RP3V kisspeptin neurons express Vgat in adult mice (Cravo et al., 2011; Cheong et al., 2015) although it is very likely that all RP3V kisspeptin neurons express VGAT during development and, as such, will all express Cas9 as adults.
evidence: Supported by citations to Cravo et al., 2011; Cheong et al., 2015

claim: All RP3V kisspeptin neurons likely express VGAT during development and will all express Cas9 as adults.
source: Prior estimates have indicated that 20–75% of RP3V kisspeptin neurons express Vgat in adult mice (Cravo et al., 2011; Cheong et al., 2015) although it is very likely that all RP3V kisspeptin neurons express VGAT during development and, as such, will all express Cas9 as adults.
evidence: Based on inference from developmental expression patterns and citations to Cravo et al., 2011; Cheong et al., 2015

claim: The almost complete lack of kisspeptin immunoreactivity is due to the critical dependence of kisspeptin expression on ESR1 in RP3V kisspeptin neurons.
source: The almost complete lack of kisspeptin immunoreactivity is due to the critical dependence of kisspeptin expression on ESR1 in RP3V kisspeptin neurons (Smith et al., 2005; Dubois et al., 2015; Greenwald-Yarnell et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2005; Dubois et al., 2015; Greenwald-Yarnell et al., 2016

claim: The two gRNA groups with normal RP3V kisspeptin expression ('lacZ' and 'normal') exhibited normal estrous cycles 3 weeks after AAV injection.
source: The two gRNA groups with normal RP3V kisspeptin expression ('lacZ' and 'normal') exhibited normal estrous cycles 3 weeks after AAV injection (Figure 5), the usual variable LH surge levels (4.8±1.7 and 6.3±1.3 ng/mL; range 0.1–14.3 ng/mL) (Figure 5) and ~40–50% of GnRH neurons with cFos at the time of the expected LH surge (Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'lacZ' and 'normal' groups exhibited the usual variable LH surge levels (4.8±1.7 and 6.3±1.3 ng/mL; range 0.1–14.3 ng/mL).
source: The two gRNA groups with normal RP3V kisspeptin expression ('lacZ' and 'normal') exhibited normal estrous cycles 3 weeks after AAV injection (Figure 5), the usual variable LH surge levels (4.8±1.7 and 6.3±1.3 ng/mL; range 0.1–14.3 ng/mL) (Figure 5) and ~40–50% of GnRH neurons with cFos at the time of the expected LH surge (Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'lacZ' and 'normal' groups had ~40–50% of GnRH neurons with cFos at the time of the expected LH surge.
source: The two gRNA groups with normal RP3V kisspeptin expression ('lacZ' and 'normal') exhibited normal estrous cycles 3 weeks after AAV injection (Figure 5), the usual variable LH surge levels (4.8±1.7 and 6.3±1.3 ng/mL; range 0.1–14.3 ng/mL) (Figure 5) and ~40–50% of GnRH neurons with cFos at the time of the expected LH surge (Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'bilateral' mice with essentially no RP3V kisspeptin expression were all found to enter constant estrus.
source: In contrast, the 'bilateral' mice with essentially no RP3V kisspeptin expression were all found to enter constant estrus (Figures 2 and 5) and have both low LH levels (1.4±0.3 ng/mL; range 0.8–2.1 ng/mL) and low cFos expression in GnRH neurons (4.3 ± 2.6%; p=0.0004, H=18.24, Kruskal-Wallis with p=0.0185 post hoc Dunn's test) (Figure 5) at the time of the expected surge.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 5

claim: The 'bilateral' mice had low LH levels (1.4±0.3 ng/mL; range 0.8–2.1 ng/mL) at the time of the expected surge.
source: In contrast, the 'bilateral' mice with essentially no RP3V kisspeptin expression were all found to enter constant estrus (Figures 2 and 5) and have both low LH levels (1.4±0.3 ng/mL; range 0.8–2.1 ng/mL) and low cFos expression in GnRH neurons (4.3 ± 2.6%; p=0.0004, H=18.24, Kruskal-Wallis with p=0.0185 post hoc Dunn's test) (Figure 5) at the time of the expected surge.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'bilateral' mice had low cFos expression in GnRH neurons (4.3 ± 2.6%) at the time of the expected surge.
source: In contrast, the 'bilateral' mice with essentially no RP3V kisspeptin expression were all found to enter constant estrus (Figures 2 and 5) and have both low LH levels (1.4±0.3 ng/mL; range 0.8–2.1 ng/mL) and low cFos expression in GnRH neurons (4.3 ± 2.6%; p=0.0004, H=18.24, Kruskal-Wallis with p=0.0185 post hoc Dunn's test) (Figure 5) at the time of the expected surge.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: Pulsatile LH release in 'bilateral' mice was variable with one mouse having no pulses in the 180 min recording period while the others displayed pulses not significantly different to gRNA-lacZ mice.
source: Pulsatile LH release in 'bilateral' mice was variable with one mouse having no pulses in the 180 min recording period while the others displayed pulses not significantly different to gRNA-lacZ mice despite an apparent trend for reduced LH pulse amplitude (p=0.1409) (Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'unilateral' mice displayed estrous cyclicity that was normal except for one mouse that went into constant diestrus.
source: Finally, the 'unilateral' mice displayed a phenotype intermediate between that of 'normal' and 'bilateral' groups. Estrous cyclicity was normal (Figure 5) except for one mouse that went into constant diestrus and LH pulsatility was unaffected (Figure 5), while LH levels (1.6±0.5 ng/mL) and the % GnRH neurons with cFos (10.3 ± 3.7%, p=0.0297, post hoc Dunn's tests) at the time of the expected LH surge were similar to the 'bilateral' group.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The 'unilateral' mice had LH levels (1.6±0.5 ng/mL) and % GnRH neurons with cFos (10.3 ± 3.7%) at the time of the expected LH surge similar to the 'bilateral' group.
source: Finally, the 'unilateral' mice displayed a phenotype intermediate between that of 'normal' and 'bilateral' groups. Estrous cyclicity was normal (Figure 5) except for one mouse that went into constant diestrus and LH pulsatility was unaffected (Figure 5), while LH levels (1.6±0.5 ng/mL) and the % GnRH neurons with cFos (10.3 ± 3.7%, p=0.0297, post hoc Dunn's tests) at the time of the expected LH surge were similar to the 'bilateral' group.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: gRNA-2 and gRNA-3 are effective at knocking down ESR1 expression in preoptic GABA neurons in adult female mice, achieving a 60–70% reduction in ESR1 within the RP3V and MPN compared to gRNA-lacZ mice.
source: We show here that gRNA-2 and gRNA-3 are effective at knocking down ESR1 expression in preoptic GABA neurons in adult female mice; both gRNA achieved a 60–70% reduction in ESR1 within the RP3V and MPN compared to gRNA-lacZ mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study

claim: gRNA-3 generated an 80% knockdown in ESR1 within arcuate kisspeptin neurons.
source: We had previously reported that gRNA-3 generated an 80% knockdown in ESR1 within arcuate kisspeptin neurons (McQuillan et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to McQuillan et al., 2022

claim: Expression of ESR1 in RP3V GABA neurons correlated positively with the percentage of GnRH neurons expressing cFos at the time of the surge.
source: When examined on the basis of the original GABA neuron groupings, the only significant observation was that expression of ESR1 in RP3V GABA neurons correlated positively with the percentage of GnRH neurons expressing cFos at the time of the surge.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: ESR1 in RP3V GABA neurons is required for normal activation of the GnRH neurons at the time of the surge.
source: While providing evidence that ESR1 in RP3V GABA neurons was required for normal activation of the GnRH neurons at the time of the surge, this was not the case for the LH surge.
evidence: Based on inference from correlation data between ESR1 expression and GnRH neuron activation

claim: Single-point LH measurements are unreliable even for the OVX+E2 paradigm with individual mice exhibiting quite marked variability in surge onset and peak LH levels.
source: We note that single-point LH measurements are unreliable even for the OVX+E2 paradigm with individual mice exhibiting quite marked variability in surge onset and peak LH levels (Czieselsky et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Czieselsky et al., 2016

claim: cFos expression in GnRH neurons is a more reliable index of whether the surge has commenced at the time of investigation than single-point LH measurements.
source: As such, we favor cFos expression in GnRH neurons as a more reliable index of whether the surge has commenced at the time of investigation.
evidence: Based on inference from the variability of LH measurements

claim: Mice with a near-complete loss of kisspeptin immunoreactivity displayed constant estrus and failed to exhibit surge activation but retained pulsatile LH secretion.
source: mice with a near-complete loss of kisspeptin immunoreactivity displayed constant estrus and failed to exhibit surge activation but retained pulsatile luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study

claim: ESR1-expressing GABA-kisspeptin neurons in the RP3V are essential for the murine preovulatory LH surge mechanism.
source: These observations demonstrate that ESR1-expressing GABA-kisspeptin neurons in the RP3V are essential for the murine preovulatory LH surge mechanism.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing loss of surge in mice with bilateral loss of kisspeptin

claim: 30–50% reductions in RP3V kisspeptin neuron number are compatible with a normal surge mechanism.
source: Prior studies have indicated that 30–50% reductions in RP3V kisspeptin neuron number are compatible with a normal surge mechanism (Szymanski and Bakker, 2012; Hu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Szymanski and Bakker, 2012; Hu et al., 2015

claim: A substantial reduction in RP3V kisspeptin input to GnRH neurons from one side of the brain may result in weaker surge activation.
source: It is possible that a substantial reduction in RP3V kisspeptin input to GnRH neurons from one side of the brain results in weaker surge activation.
evidence: Based on speculation about the effects of unilateral kisspeptin reduction

claim: Unilateral reduction in RP3V kisspeptin may alter the timing of surge onset outside the window examined in this study.

source: This observation agrees with the 'two-compartment model' of the GnRH neuron network in which the kisspeptin pulse and kisspeptin surge generators are thought to operate in relative independence at different compartments of the female GnRH neuron to bring about LH pulses and the LH surge, respectively (Herbison, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Herbison, 2020

evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study

source: These observations provide definitive evidence for ESR1-expressing RP3V GABA-kisspeptin neurons being essential for the preovulatory surge mechanism while having no role in pulse generation.

claim: In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 editing achieved a 60–70% knockdown in ESR1 expression by GABA neurons located within the RP3V and MPN in adult female mice.
source: In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 editing was used to achieve a 60–70% knockdown in estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) expression by GABA neurons located within the regions of the rostral periventricular area of the third ventricle (RP3V) and medial preoptic nuclei (MPN) in adult female mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study

claim: Mice with bilateral ESR1 deletion in RP3V GABA neurons had reduced cFos expression in GnRH neurons at the time of the surge.

evidence: Supported by experimental data from the study

claim: The preoptic area has a predominant GABAergic phenotype of neurons.
source: In keeping with the predominant GABAergic phenotype of preoptic area neurons (Moffitt et al., 2018), large numbers of cells expressing EGFP/Cas9 were detected throughout the region (Figure 1A and B), including the AVPV, PVpo, MPN, and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.
evidence: Supported by citation to Moffitt et al., 2018

claim: Up to one half of medial preoptic area GABA neurons express ESR1.
source: In keeping with prior studies showing that up to one half of medial preoptic area GABA neurons express ESR1 (Herbison, 1997; Cheong et al., 2015), we found in gRNA-LacZ mice that 54.9 ± 3.7% and 59.7 ± 3.9% of VGAT-EGFP neurons in the RP3V (N=6) and MPN (N=7), respectively, were immunoreactive for ESR1 (Figure 1A and C).
evidence: Supported by citations to Herbison, 1997; Cheong et al., 2015
